text:
Mason McTavish came to St. Louis from Anaheim with a promise attached: a bigger job. He has it. He is on the ice for 65% of the Blues' power-play chances, up from 36% last season, and his own chances are up to 1.65 expected goals per 60 from 1.22. That is why our numbers flag him as a breakout candidate at 23.

The results have gone cold, though. After a fast start he has three points in his last ten games against 6.3 expected, the kind of dip The Hockey News picked up on this month. Seven goals on 7.99 expected for the season says the finishing is roughly fair; the recent drought looks more like bad luck on the chances than a lack of them, since he keeps shooting (48 shots).

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the better setup men last season, and Evolving-Hockey liked his offense while flagging his defense (bottom 2% of forwards for chances against). The role is real. The two-way game is what we'd watch.
headline: McTavish's bigger role hasn't found the net lately
